:::{#exm-entropy-quantized-uniform}
#### Quantizing a uniform random variable

Let $X$ be [uniformly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform) between $0$ and $1$,
and let the bin width be $\Delta = 1/n$ for a positive whole number $n$.
Then $X^\Delta$ takes each of $n$ values with [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) $1/n$,
so by @thm-entropy-discrete, its [entropy](#def-entropy) is

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} = -n \cdot \tfrac{1}{n} \log \tfrac{1}{n} = \log n = -\log \Delta.$$

Hence $\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta = 0$,
which equals $\entropyf{X} = 0$.
The [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) of $X$ jumps at $0$ and $1$,
so it is not [continuous](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-continuous),
and @thm-entropy-quantization does not apply as stated.
Its conclusion still holds here,
because the density takes one value on every bin.
Measured in [bits](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/entropy.html#def-bit), with $n = 2^k$,
the entropy is $k$.
It tends to $\infty$ as $k$ grows,
which agrees with @cor-entropy-quantization-diverges
[@cover2006elements, Example 8.3.1].
